title: Localise for 12+ locales with RTL, Indic scripts and pseudo-loc CI
body:
## Context
Sane Notes must be usable, and feel native, in the locked locale list (CLAUDE.md decision 10): English first, then Hindi + major Indian languages, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional as distinct locales), Korean and Arabic (RTL). This epic owns the whole localisation surface defined in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 (PRD-CO-370..377) and researched in `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11: the Flutter `intl`/ARB pipeline, the supported-locale list and resolution, RTL chrome mirroring, locale-aware dates/numbers/currency (including ₹ lakh/crore grouping), on-demand handwriting-recognition language packs, font fallback for CJK/Indic/Arabic scripts, the in-app language picker, the translation workflow, and a pseudo-localisation CI gate. India-first is a market wedge: `docs/research/sources/user-pain-points-and-market-gaps.md` names English-only OCR as gap #3, and Indic handwriting recognition (PRD-CO-373) directly attacks it. Localisation is cross-cutting — the pipeline and pseudo-loc gate land in M1 so every string is externalised from the first UI, while full RTL/Arabic and translation QA are audited in M7 (`docs/roadmap.md`, PRD-04 header). Standing constraint: UI language never alters user note content (PRD-CO-377).

## Scope
**In:** the ARB pipeline; locale list + resolution; pseudo-locale CI gate; date/number/currency formatting; RTL layout mirroring; font fallback bundling; platform IME support; handwriting language-pack UX; the language picker; translation workflow & QA; the multilingual/RTL audit. Coordinated across `app/lib/l10n`, `packages/sane_ui`, and `packages/sane_ml` adapters.
**Out:** the accessibility (a11y) work (its own epic — reading fonts, screen readers, contrast), the AI translation feature itself (PRD-CO-156, owned by the Sane Sage AI epic), store-listing copy translation (release epic), and the recognition engine internals (owned by the handwriting/OCR epic; this epic owns only the language-selection and pack-download UX layered on top).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every child issue below is closed and its acceptance criteria met.
- [ ] `flutter gen-l10n` builds and the app renders with zero hard-coded user-facing strings (arch-lint/grep gate clean).
- [ ] Switching to Arabic mirrors all chrome while the ink canvas stays un-mirrored; switching to Hindi/Tamil/Japanese/zh-Hant renders with no tofu glyphs.
- [ ] The pseudo-locale (en-XA/en-XB) CI job is a release gate and passes with no truncation, overlap, hard-coded English or broken mirroring.
- [ ] `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` resolve as distinct locales and differ on screen.
- [ ] Indian locale shows ₹ with 1,00,000-style grouping; no note content is ever auto-translated by a UI language change.

## Technical notes
Pipeline per `accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 "Flutter intl / ARB workflow": `flutter_localizations` + `intl`, `flutter: generate: true`, `l10n.yaml`, ARB with typed placeholders + ICU plurals/select, `untranslated-messages-file`, `use-deferred-loading: true` for web. Strings live in `app/lib/l10n`; `sane_ui` exposes localised component copy via delegates but stays a pure leaf (`docs/architecture/overview.md` §5). Handwriting packs use ML Kit Digital Ink base models (ADR-0016 §Ink→text), downloaded on demand and integrity-checked. Follows PRD-CO-370..377.

## Security & privacy
Baseline: no note content, ink coordinates or PII in logs — only opaque BCP-47 locale codes and message keys (CLAUDE.md §7.3). ARB files carry only UI strings and MUST NOT contain secrets or user content (MASVS-CODE-3). RTL/bidi rendering of untrusted note text must neutralise Unicode bidirectional-override spoofing (Trojan-Source class, CWE-1007). Downloaded language packs are integrity-verified over TLS (MASVS-NETWORK-1). Translation of note content is user-initiated only, preserving the original (MASVS-PRIVACY-1, PRD-CO-377).

## UX notes
All localisation-visible chrome follows `docs/design/design-system.md` and must render correctly across all 17 looks (Paper, Skeuomorphism, Retro, Minimalism, Glassmorphism, Flat, Material, Bento UI, Pop, Maximalism, Y2K, Cyberpunk, Neumorphism, Claymorphism, Brutalism, Neo-Brutalism, Editorial) in light and dark, and at RTL. The language picker lives in Settings → Language & Region (design Settings §12). a11y: 44pt/48dp targets, contrast tokens, keyboard reachable on web.

## Test plan
Aggregate of children: `flutter gen-l10n` build check in CI; `app/test/l10n/` unit tests for resolution/formatting; pseudo-locale integration run; golden tests per look at LTR and RTL under `app/test/golden/i18n/`. Each child names its own files.

## Dependencies
Depends on {{SN-FND-002}} (monorepo scaffold), {{SN-FND-004}} (workspace + lints), {{SN-CI-001}} (CI to host the pseudo-loc gate). Children depend on {{SN-DS-003}}, {{SN-TXT-001}}, {{SN-HWR-001}}, {{SN-SET-001}}, {{SN-BILL-001}} as noted.

## Definition of done
- [ ] All child issues merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, gen-l10n, pseudo-loc gate, security scans).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (localisation pipeline documented in `docs/architecture/overview.md`).
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

### Children
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-002}} Establish the Flutter intl/ARB pipeline
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-003}} Define the supported-locale list and resolution
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-004}} Pseudo-locale (en-XA/en-XB) CI gate
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-005}} Locale-aware date and number formatting
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-006}} ₹ currency formatting and per-storefront tiers
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-007}} RTL chrome mirroring
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-008}} Font fallback for CJK/Indic/Arabic scripts
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-009}} Platform IME support in text fields
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-010}} Handwriting recognition language-pack UX
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-011}} In-app language picker
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-012}} Translation workflow, glossary and QA handoff
- [ ] {{SN-I18N-013}} RTL and multilingual layout audit

title: Establish the Flutter intl/ARB localisation pipeline
body:
## Context
Every user-facing string in the app must be externalised from day one so translation, pseudo-localisation and RTL all become mechanical rather than a retrofit. This issue stands up the Flutter `intl`/ARB pipeline exactly as specified in `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 "Flutter intl / ARB workflow" and required by PRD-CO-371 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9. Without it, later work (locale list, pseudo-loc gate, translation handoff, currency formatting) has nowhere to live. It is the foundation the rest of the {{SN-I18N-001}} epic builds on, and it must be in place before any editor chrome ships strings in M1 (`docs/roadmap.md` M1 "App shell + adaptive layout").

## Scope
**In:** add `flutter_localizations` (SDK) + `intl` to `app/`; set `flutter: generate: true` in `app/pubspec.yaml`; author `app/l10n.yaml` (`arb-dir: lib/l10n`, `template-arb-file: app_en.arb`, `output-localization-file: app_localizations.dart`, `output-class: AppLocalizations`, `use-escaping: true`, `untranslated-messages-file: l10n/untranslated.json`, `use-deferred-loading: true`); create the `app_en.arb` template with `@`-metadata, typed placeholders (with `format` for date/number/currency), and at least one ICU plural and one select/gender example; wire `localizationsDelegates` (`AppLocalizations.delegate` + Global Material/Cupertino/Widgets delegates) and `supportedLocales` into the root `MaterialApp`; add a lint/grep gate that fails CI on hard-coded user-facing string literals in widgets.
**Out:** the full locale list and resolution logic ({{SN-I18N-003}}), pseudo-locale build ({{SN-I18N-004}}), actual translated ARB files (translation workflow {{SN-I18N-012}}), and formatting utilities ({{SN-I18N-005}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `flutter gen-l10n` (and `flutter run`) generates `AppLocalizations` with no errors.
- [ ] Reading a string is `AppLocalizations.of(context)!.key(args)`; no widget contains a hard-coded user-facing literal (CI grep/analyzer gate red on violation).
- [ ] The template ARB contains a working ICU plural (`{count, plural, =0{…} =1{…} other{…}}`) and a select/gender message, both rendering correctly in a widget test.
- [ ] `untranslated-messages-file` is generated and tracked; an empty report is the release condition.
- [ ] `use-deferred-loading: true` is set so web can lazy-load locales (verified: only `app_en` bundle loads on first paint).
- [ ] `dart analyze --fatal-infos` and `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` pass on generated + hand-written code.

## Technical notes
Files: `app/pubspec.yaml`, `app/l10n.yaml`, `app/lib/l10n/app_en.arb`, generated `app/lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart` (git-ignored per convention or committed per repo policy — follow `docs/architecture/overview.md`). `sane_ui` stays a pure leaf (overview §5): component copy is passed in from `app/`, never imported the other way. Keep message keys `lowerCamelCase` (CLAUDE.md §6). The hard-coded-string gate can reuse the arch-lint tooling from {{SN-FND-004}}. Implements PRD-CO-371.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. ARB files hold only UI strings — no secrets, tokens, keys or note content may ever be placed in them (CLAUDE.md §7.2, MASVS-CODE-3). No content or PII in logs; only message keys and locale codes may be logged (MASVS-PRIVACY-1). `use-escaping: true` avoids ICU-syntax breakage from apostrophes.

## UX notes
No new screen; this is plumbing. It must not regress first-paint. Once in place, all chrome copy across the 17 looks flows through `AppLocalizations`, so a look change never re-hard-codes text. a11y unaffected; strings remain announceable by screen readers via the same widgets.

## Test plan
Unit/widget: `app/test/l10n/app_localizations_test.dart` (plural + select render correctly; `of(context)` returns the template locale). CI step: `flutter gen-l10n` build check + the hard-coded-string grep gate in `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` (or the Flutter CI workflow). Manual: run app, confirm strings resolve.

## Dependencies
{{SN-FND-002}} (Flutter monorepo scaffold with `app/`), {{SN-FND-004}} (workspace + very_good_analysis lints and arch-lint tooling).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, gen-l10n build, hard-coded-string gate).
- [ ] Docs updated: localisation pipeline noted in `docs/architecture/overview.md` and the agent onboarding.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

title: Define supported-locale list and locale resolution
body:
## Context
The app must declare exactly the locked locale list and resolve the device/user locale to the best supported match, including the subtle cases that trip apps up: `zh-Hans` vs `zh-Hant` as genuinely distinct locales, and script/region subtags. PRD-CO-370 in `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §9 and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("CJK & complex-text input") require `Locale.fromSubtags(languageCode:'zh', scriptCode:'Hans'|'Hant')`. Getting resolution right underpins every downstream feature — fonts, RTL, recognition packs and formatting all key off the resolved locale. This is a direct child of {{SN-I18N-001}} and depends on the pipeline from {{SN-I18N-002}}.

## Scope
**In:** define `supportedLocales` = English (`en`), Hindi (`hi`) + priority Indian languages (Bengali `bn`, Gujarati `gu`, Kannada `kn`, Malayalam `ml`, Marathi `mr`, Punjabi `pa`, Tamil `ta`, Telugu `te`, Odia `or`), Spanish `es`, German `de`, French `fr`, Portuguese `pt`, Japanese `ja`, Chinese Simplified `zh-Hans`, Chinese Traditional `zh-Hant`, Korean `ko`, Arabic `ar`; a `localeResolutionCallback`/`localeListResolutionCallback` that maps an unsupported device locale to the closest supported one (language+script match before language-only, English fallback); a central `SupportedLocale` model (native name, English name, BCP-47 tag, text direction) for use by the picker and settings; declare the priority/phasing (which locales are release-blocking vs on-demand) in a doc note.
**Out:** the actual translated ARB files ({{SN-I18N-012}}), the picker UI ({{SN-I18N-011}}), RTL mirroring ({{SN-I18N-007}}), and per-locale fonts ({{SN-I18N-008}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `MaterialApp.supportedLocales` contains all locked locales with `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` as separate `Locale.fromSubtags` entries; a widget test proves they resolve distinctly.
- [ ] A device set to an unsupported locale (e.g. `it-IT`) resolves to English; a device set to `zh-TW` resolves to `zh-Hant`, `zh-CN` to `zh-Hans`.
- [ ] Arabic (`ar`) resolves with `TextDirection.rtl`; all others LTR (per the `SupportedLocale` model).
- [ ] Resolution logic is unit-tested for language-only, language+script, and region-only inputs.
- [ ] The `SupportedLocale` list exposes a human-readable native name (e.g. "हिन्दी", "日本語", "العربية") for the picker.

## Technical notes
Use Flutter `Locale`/`Locale.fromSubtags`, `WidgetsApp.localeListResolutionCallback` (prefer the list form to honour the OS preferred-locale order). Keep the `SupportedLocale` model and resolver in `app/lib/l10n/supported_locales.dart`. Record the India-priority set from `accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 Indic list. Note in `docs/architecture/overview.md` (or a short ADR) which locales are release-blocking for v1 vs deferred, since the maintainer has not fixed the phasing (decide sensibly: `en` first, `hi` + `ar` next for RTL/India coverage, rest as translations complete). Implements PRD-CO-370.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. The resolved locale is derived from OS settings; treat any locale value arriving via deep link or import as untrusted and validate it against `supportedLocales` before use (fall back to English) — never let an external caller force an arbitrary `Locale` string into formatting/logging paths (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). Log locale codes only, never note content (MASVS-PRIVACY-1).

## UX notes
Native language names must display in their own script (needs the font work {{SN-I18N-008}} to avoid tofu, so order the picker to degrade gracefully before fonts land). The list ordering: device/best-match first, then alphabetical by native name. Applies across all 17 looks; the picker itself is {{SN-I18N-011}}. a11y: each locale row exposes its English name as a semantics label so screen readers in any language can announce it.

## Test plan
Unit: `app/test/l10n/locale_resolution_test.dart` (unsupported→en, zh-TW→zh-Hant, zh-CN→zh-Hans, region-only, script fallback, RTL flag on `ar`). Widget: `MaterialApp` built with a forced locale resolves as expected. Manual: change device language to Arabic and Traditional Chinese, confirm resolution.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-002}} (ARB pipeline + delegates).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit).
- [ ] Docs updated: locale phasing note added to `docs/architecture/overview.md` or a short ADR.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

title: Add pseudo-locale build and CI truncation/mirroring gate
body:
## Context
Pseudo-localisation catches i18n defects (truncation, hard-coded English, broken concatenation, RTL mirroring bugs) before any human translation exists, and does so continuously in CI. PRD-CO-376 makes a pseudo-locale build a hard release gate, and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("Pseudo-localisation testing") specifies the exact transforms: ~40% string expansion, Latin accenting, Greek/Cyrillic/Indic padding for font coverage, delimiter wrapping, and the ICU `en-XA` (accents) + `en-XB` (bidi/RTL mirror) pseudo-locales — never hijacking a real locale tag. This gate protects every locale we later add and is the cheapest place to find layout breaks. Child of {{SN-I18N-001}}; needs the pipeline {{SN-I18N-002}} and CI from {{SN-CI-001}}.

## Scope
**In:** generate `app_en-XA.arb` (accented + ~40% expansion + `^…^` delimiter wrapping) and `app_en-XB.arb` (bidi/RTL mirror) from the template ARB via a `tools/scripts/` generator; register `en-XA`/`en-XB` in `supportedLocales` for non-release builds only; a CI job (in the Flutter CI / `devsecops.yml`) that builds the app in each pseudo-locale, drives the key screens, and fails on: text truncation/overflow (RenderFlex overflow, clipped Text), any string still rendering as plain English (unwrapped by `^…^`), and broken mirroring in `en-XB`; wire the job as a release-blocking gate.
**Out:** real translations ({{SN-I18N-012}}), RTL production behaviour for Arabic ({{SN-I18N-007}}), and font coverage fixes surfaced by the padding (those flow to {{SN-I18N-008}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `tools/scripts/gen_pseudo_arb.dart` (or `.mjs`) regenerates `en-XA`/`en-XB` deterministically from `app_en.arb` and is idempotent.
- [ ] `en-XA` expands strings ≥40% (1–2 word strings more), accents Latin text, pads with Greek/Cyrillic/Indic glyphs, and wraps each string in `^…^`.
- [ ] `en-XB` mirrors layout (bidi) so any hard left/right (non-directional) inset is visibly wrong.
- [ ] The CI job renders the top screens (Library, Editor chrome, Settings, Share overlay, Upgrade) in both pseudo-locales and fails on any overflow, any unwrapped English string, or broken mirroring.
- [ ] The job is marked a required check / release gate and is green on the current UI.
- [ ] Pseudo-locales never appear in a release build (guarded to `kDebugMode`/flavour).

## Technical notes
Use the ICU/Flutter-recognised `en-XA`/`en-XB` tags (do not reuse a real locale). Rendering assertions can use `integration_test` + golden/overflow detection, or a widget harness that pumps each route and asserts no `FlutterError` overflow and that every visible `Text` starts/ends with the `^` sentinel. Keep the generator in `tools/` (not shipped). Reference PRD-CO-376 and the pipeline from {{SN-I18N-002}}. The gate belongs alongside the other CI scanners from {{SN-CI-001}}.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. The generator only transforms UI strings; it must never emit secrets or content and must fail if the template ARB somehow contains a non-string placeholder value (MASVS-CODE-3). Pseudo-locale artefacts stay out of release binaries.

## UX notes
No user-facing UX; this is a developer gate. It protects the 17 looks by catching per-look overflow (dense looks like Brutalism/Editorial with tight spacing break first). Screens driven mirror the design (`docs/design/screens-and-flows.md`): Library home, Editor palette dock, Settings §12, Share overlay §10, Upgrade §13.

## Test plan
Infra test: run the generator, diff output is stable; the CI job passes on clean UI and fails on a deliberately truncated test widget (a regression fixture under `app/integration_test/pseudo_locale_test.dart`). Manual: run app in `en-XA` and eyeball a screen.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-002}} (ARB template + delegates), {{SN-CI-001}} (CI pipeline to host the gate).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green; the pseudo-loc job is a required check.
- [ ] Docs updated: the gate documented in the DevSecOps/QA docs.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

title: Implement locale-aware date and number formatting
body:
## Context
Every date and number the app shows (recents timestamps, page counts, audio durations, file sizes, study stats, "last edited") must be formatted through `intl` so it reads correctly in each locale — never hand-concatenated. PRD-CO-375 and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("Locale-aware dates, numbers & ₹ pricing") require `DateFormat`/`NumberFormat` with the resolved locale and forbid hand-formatting. This issue delivers the shared formatting helpers the whole app uses; currency (₹) is split into {{SN-I18N-006}} because it also touches billing/store tiers. Child of {{SN-I18N-001}}, built on the pipeline {{SN-I18N-002}} and the resolved locale from {{SN-I18N-003}}.

## Scope
**In:** a `SaneFormat` helper (in `app/lib/l10n/` or a small formatting util) wrapping `intl` `DateFormat` (`yMd`, `yMMMMd`, `jm`, relative "2 hours ago" via a small relative-time helper) and `NumberFormat` (`decimalPattern`, `compact`, `percentPattern`) bound to the active locale; a CI/analyzer rule (or code-review checklist entry) that flags direct `toString()` of DateTime/num in widgets; wire existing chrome (recents, page counts, durations) through it.
**Out:** currency/₹ formatting and store price tiers ({{SN-I18N-006}}); translated month/day names come free from `intl` locale data — just ensure the data is loaded.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dates render per locale: `en` shows `Sep 13, 2026`; `de` shows `13.09.2026`; `ja` shows `2026年9月13日`; `ar` shows Arabic-Indic digits where the locale dictates.
- [ ] Numbers group per locale (`1,234` en vs `1.234` de) and durations/percentages format via `intl`, not string math.
- [ ] A relative-time helper returns localised "just now / N minutes ago / yesterday".
- [ ] No widget calls `DateTime.toString()`/`num.toString()` for display (gate or review-checklist item present).
- [ ] Formatting reads the active locale from context and updates when the locale changes (widget test).

## Technical notes
Ensure `intl` locale data is initialised for supported locales (Flutter loads it via `flutter_localizations`; verify `Intl.defaultLocale`/`Localizations.localeOf(context)` drive `DateFormat(pattern, locale)`). Keep helpers pure and testable. Reference PRD-CO-375; the ₹ path is deliberately deferred to {{SN-I18N-006}}. Files: `app/lib/l10n/sane_format.dart`, `app/test/l10n/sane_format_test.dart`.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. Timestamps shown are note metadata, not content; still, never log formatted user timestamps tied to identifiable content (MASVS-PRIVACY-1). Guard against locale-injection: format only with a validated supported locale ({{SN-I18N-003}}).

## UX notes
Formatting is visible in the Library recents, Editor status, audio bar and study stats across all 17 looks; ensure digit width doesn't break tight looks (Editorial/Brutalism) — numbers use tabular figures where the design token provides them. a11y: screen readers read the localised string, so no separate handling needed.

## Test plan
Unit: `app/test/l10n/sane_format_test.dart` (date/number/percent/relative-time across `en`, `de`, `ja`, `hi`, `ar`). Widget: a label re-renders on locale change. Manual: switch locale, view recents.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-002}} (pipeline), {{SN-I18N-003}} (locale resolution).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit).
- [ ] Docs updated if a formatting convention is added to the coding standards.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

title: Implement rupee currency formatting with lakh/crore grouping
body:
## Context
Sane Notes prices in ₹ (design reference ₹83/month, ₹999/year) and targets India first, so pricing surfaces must show the ₹ symbol with Indian lakh/crore digit grouping (1,00,000) driven by locale, not hard-coded, and store tiers must be set per storefront rather than FX-converted. PRD-CO-375 and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("Locale-aware dates, numbers & ₹ pricing") require `NumberFormat.simpleCurrency(locale: 'en_IN' | 'hi_IN')` and per-storefront App Store/Play tiers. This complements the general formatting in {{SN-I18N-005}} but is separate because it binds to the billing surface ({{SN-BILL-001}}) and needs store credentials. Child of {{SN-I18N-001}}.

## Scope
**In:** a currency formatter using `NumberFormat.simpleCurrency`/`currency` bound to the active locale (₹ for `en_IN`/`hi_IN` with lakh/crore grouping; correct symbol + grouping for other storefronts); apply it to every price/plan string (Upgrade overlay §13, plan matrix §14, billing/entitlement screens); document the per-storefront price-tier mapping (App Store Connect / Play Console tier IDs) so displayed prices match the actual charged tier; a fallback that formats from the platform IAP product's own localized price string when available (source of truth for charged amount).
**Out:** the entitlement/purchase flow itself ({{SN-BILL-001}}), student-verification pricing logic, and non-currency number formatting ({{SN-I18N-005}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Indian locale renders `₹1,00,000`-style grouping (lakh/crore), verified on-device (grouping is a property of `en_IN`/`hi_IN`).
- [ ] Prices come from the platform IAP product's localized price where a purchase path exists; the `intl` formatter is used only for display of known reference amounts and non-store contexts.
- [ ] Every price string in Upgrade §13 and plan matrix §14 formats via the helper — no hard-coded "₹83".
- [ ] Non-INR storefronts show their own currency + grouping (e.g. `$`, `€`) via the same helper.
- [ ] Price-tier mapping is documented and the displayed price never contradicts the charged price (test with at least IN + one other storefront).

## Technical notes
`NumberFormat.simpleCurrency(locale: Localizations.localeOf(context).toString())`; for India force `en_IN`/`hi_IN` grouping. The authoritative charged amount is the store product's `price`/`priceString` from the billing plugin — prefer it; use `intl` for reference/marketing copy. Store tiers are configured in App Store Connect / Google Play Console (maintainer credentials → `needs-credentials`). Files: `app/lib/l10n/currency_format.dart`, integrate with `packages/sane_billing` product models. Implements PRD-CO-375; coordinate with {{SN-BILL-001}}.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. Never trust a client-formatted price as the charge; the store is the source of truth (fail-open to free never charges, CLAUDE.md M8). No PII/purchase identifiers in logs (MASVS-PRIVACY-1). Store credentials are injected via CI secrets, never committed (CLAUDE.md §7.2).

## UX notes
Prices appear in the Upgrade overlay (design §13) and plan matrix (§14) across all 17 looks and both themes; ₹ glyph must render in every look's display font (coordinate with {{SN-I18N-008}} font coverage). a11y: price strings read naturally by screen readers (e.g. "eighty-three rupees per month" via the localized string). Empty/error state: if the store price is unavailable, show the reference price with a subtle "prices may vary by region" note, never a broken/zero price.

## Test plan
Unit: `app/test/l10n/currency_format_test.dart` (₹ lakh/crore grouping for `en_IN`/`hi_IN`; `$`/`€` for other locales). Widget: Upgrade overlay renders store price when present, reference price otherwise. Manual: sandbox IAP in an Indian and a non-Indian storefront.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-005}} (number formatting base), {{SN-BILL-001}} (billing/entitlements + IAP product models). Store price tiers require maintainer credentials.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit).
- [ ] Docs updated: per-storefront price-tier mapping documented.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.

title: Mirror app chrome for RTL locales without mirroring the canvas
body:
## Context
Arabic (and later Hebrew/Urdu/Persian) require the app chrome to mirror right-to-left, while the ink canvas must never mirror — a drawing is a drawing. PRD-CO-372 and `docs/research/sources/accessibility-i18n-and-inclusive-design.md` §11 ("RTL layouts") specify mirroring via `Directionality`/`EdgeInsetsDirectional`/`AlignmentDirectional`, an un-mirrored canvas, and RTL being independent from the left-handed toggle so the two compose correctly. Getting this right early (M1) prevents a costly retrofit and is validated continuously by the `en-XB` pseudo-locale gate ({{SN-I18N-004}}). Child of {{SN-I18N-001}}; depends on the locale model {{SN-I18N-003}} and the component library {{SN-DS-003}}.

## Scope
**In:** replace hard left/right paddings, alignments and positioned offsets in chrome with directional equivalents (`EdgeInsetsDirectional`, `AlignmentDirectional`, `PositionedDirectional`, `TextAlign.start/end`); ensure the palette dock, page rail, Library grid, Settings, Share and Upgrade overlays mirror under `ar`; wrap the ink `CustomPainter`/editor canvas host in an explicit `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr)` (or equivalent) so strokes and page coordinates are never mirrored; make the RTL mirroring and the left-handed page-rail toggle (design Settings §12 `prefs.leftHanded`, PRD-CO-337) independent settings that compose; neutralise Unicode bidi-override control characters when rendering untrusted note/OCR text in chrome (comment previews, search snippets).
**Out:** actual Arabic translations ({{SN-I18N-012}}), Arabic/Indic font coverage ({{SN-I18N-008}}), and the left-handed toggle implementation itself (owned by editor/settings; this issue only guarantees composition).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In `ar`, all chrome mirrors (dock, rail, nav, overlays); in `en` it is unchanged.
- [ ] The ink canvas and stroke coordinates are identical LTR and RTL — a stroke drawn top-left stays top-left (golden test).
- [ ] RTL + left-handed compose: Arabic with left-handed mode places the rail correctly and preserves focus order (no double-flip bug).
- [ ] No widget uses `EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:)` or `Alignment.centerLeft/Right` for chrome (grep/lint gate or review-checklist item).
- [ ] Search snippets / comment previews containing RTL override characters (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) render without spoofing the surrounding UI (bidi controls stripped or isolated).
- [ ] The `en-XB` pseudo-locale CI gate passes.

## Technical notes
Flutter auto-mirrors Material/Cupertino widgets under an RTL `Directionality`; the work is removing hard-coded directions in custom widgets and pinning the canvas LTR. Files: chrome widgets in `app/lib/` and `packages/sane_ui`; the editor canvas host. Bidi sanitisation: strip or wrap bidi-control codepoints before painting untrusted text (Trojan-Source/CWE-1007). Reference PRD-CO-372, PRD-CO-337 (left-handed compose), and the `en-XB` gate {{SN-I18N-004}}.

## Security & privacy
Untrusted note text (from imports, shared notebooks, OCR) rendered in chrome must not use Unicode bidirectional overrides to visually spoof UI or reorder text deceptively — strip/neutralise bidi controls (CWE-1007, MASVS-PLATFORM-2). No note content in logs (baseline). The canvas-LTR pin also prevents a mismatched coordinate space that could corrupt saved geometry.

## UX notes
Mirrors the design across all 17 looks and light/dark at RTL; the design's left-handed mode (Settings §12 "Moves the page rail to the left so your hand never covers it") must still work in Arabic. a11y: focus/traversal order follows visual order in both directions; 44pt/48dp targets unchanged. Empty/loading/error states in overlays must also mirror.

## Test plan
Golden: `app/test/golden/i18n/rtl_chrome_test.dart` (Library, Editor chrome, Settings, Share overlay in `ar`, sampled across representative looks) + a canvas golden proving no mirroring. Widget: RTL⟂left-handed composition test; bidi-override sanitisation unit test in `app/test/l10n/bidi_sanitize_test.dart`. Manual: run in Arabic with left-handed mode on.

## Dependencies
{{SN-I18N-003}} (locale + RTL flag), {{SN-DS-003}} (component library to mirror). Composes with the left-handed toggle (design Settings §12 / PRD-CO-337).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, golden, unit, en-XB gate).
- [ ] Docs updated: RTL guidance added to `docs/design/design-system.md` if a new convention is introduced.
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md.
